question: Where can I get the register of water abstraction rights and concessions in the United States, with location, holder, use, authorised volume and status?

answer.summary: There is no national register of water rights in the United States; each state creates and publishes its own. California (CalWATRS files on data.ca.gov, weekly CSV and API), Colorado (CDSS REST API, anonymous quota) and Oregon (OWRD point-of-diversion layers plus the WRIS record viewer) were tested. They give location, use, amounts and status, and each has a holder field. Vocabularies, units and row definitions differ by state. The multi-state WaDE/WestDAAT service was taken offline in October 2026.
main_caveats: No national register exists in the evidence found: rights are recorded by each state, and only California, Colorado and Oregon were tested.
California's older eWRIMS flat files are marked discontinued (not updated since July 2025); the current CalWATRS datasets cover participants and geospatial links.
Row counts are not right counts: CA rows are right-feature links, CO rows are decreed lines per structure, OR rows are point-of-diversion by use rows.
Volumes are not comparable: CA face value in acre-feet, CO CFS or AF by decree, OR mostly cfs. None measures actual extraction.
WSWC took the WaDE/WestDAAT multi-state service offline in October 2026 and directs users to state agencies, which remain authoritative.
Holder fields hold personal data; names and addresses were inspected only as counts and are not reproduced.
answer.confidence_reason: Queries were reproduced and counted in three states; the other states and any aggregators were not tested, and some counts come from sampled fields.

attributes.note: WGS84 points of diversion in CA, CO and OR; CA places of use are listed without shapes. Coordinates only, no region-wide register.
attributes.gap_note: Verified in three states only (CA, CO, OR). Other states and any national register were not tested; Utah and Idaho pages timed out and Washington returned 403 on 2026-11-24.

attributes.note: A holder field exists in CA (participants file), CO (associatedContacts) and OR (name fields, WRIS contact block); names not reproduced.
attributes.gap_note: Access conditions: CA file is open (CC BY) and includes mailing addresses; CO contacts are returned by the open API; OR name-field population was not measured. Other states and any national register were not tested; Utah and Idaho pages timed out and Washington returned 403 on 2026-11-24.

attributes.note: Use published as purposes text (CA), coded uses 0-X (CO) and use code plus group (OR); vocabularies differ by state.
attributes.gap_note: Use vocabularies were not mapped across states. Other states and any national register were not tested; Utah and Idaho pages timed out and Washington returned 403 on 2026-11-24.

attributes.note: CA face value in acre-feet; CO net amounts in CFS or AF per row; OR mostly rate in cfs with sparse acre-feet. None is actual diversion.
attributes.gap_note: CA face value is filled for 24,547 of 55,711 rights; OR acre-feet for 4,061 of 57,926 surface-irrigation rows and 85 of 23,983 groundwater-irrigation rows; CO unit mix was not measured. Other states and any national register were not tested; Utah and Idaho pages timed out and Washington returned 403 on 2026-11-24.

attributes.note: CA right status (Licensed, Revoked...), CO structure in-use code, OR WRIS status; OR GIS layers show current rights only.
attributes.gap_note: Current validity is not established by a historical grant; CO abandoned-right handling in net amounts and OR status coverage beyond one record were not tested. Other states and any national register were not tested; Utah and Idaho pages timed out and Washington returned 403 on 2026-11-24.

sources.name: CalWATRS Water Rights Geospatial Data
sources.publisher: California State Water Resources Control Board (published on data.ca.gov)
sources.format: CSV in ZIP (64.5 MB unzipped) and CKAN DataStore JSON API
sources.summary: Weekly CalWATRS file linking each California water right, application or claim to its mapped points of diversion and places of use, with coordinates, status, face value and purposes of use.
sources.coverage_note: California only. 109,480 right-feature rows covering 55,711 distinct rights/claims; 68,015 rows are points of diversion. Face value is filled for 44% of rights.
caveats: Rows are right-feature links; face value repeats on each row.
Places of use and conveyance lines are listed without geometry.

problems: The ZIP download answers with a 302 redirect before the 200.
CSV row count (109,480) matched the CKAN DataStore total.

example.example_result: HTTP 200, 6 rows for right A027261 (Licensed, face value 33,500 acre-feet) split between Point of Diversion and Point of Storage features; the face value repeats on every row.

sources.name: CalWATRS Water Rights Participants
sources.publisher: California State Water Resources Control Board (published on data.ca.gov)
sources.summary: Weekly CalWATRS file listing who is connected to each California water right (primary owner, agent, buyer and others) with the right's type, status and face value.
sources.coverage_note: California only. 157,283 relationship rows for 56,441 distinct rights/claims; 81,611 rows are primary-owner relationships. Contains personal data.
caveats: Includes names and mailing addresses: do not republish them.

problems: Only counts and category values were inspected; no participant names were read or copied.

sources.name: CDSS REST web services: water rights net amounts, transactions and structures
sources.publisher: Colorado Division of Water Resources (DWR), Colorado Decision Support Systems
sources.format: JSON (and CSV via format parameter) over a REST API
sources.summary: Colorado's REST API serves court-decreed water rights by structure with coordinates, decreed uses, absolute and conditional amounts and priority dates, plus structure status and contacts.
sources.coverage_note: Colorado only. 173,294 net-amount rows across seven divisions; anonymous quota of 1,000 calls and 600,000 rows per day.
caveats: Amounts are in CFS or acre-feet depending on the row.
Rows are decreed lines, not distinct rights.

problems: A decreedUnits filter was ignored by netamount (row count unchanged), so unit mix was not measured.
Abandoned-right handling in net amounts was not tested.

example.example_result: HTTP 200 JSON with 8 net-amount rows for structure WDID 0400588 (ditch, Boulder County): decreedUses, decreedUnits C, netAbsolute values, appropriation dates 1875-1987, lat 40.259 lon -105.176.

sources.name: Oregon water rights by type and use: Points of Diversion layers
sources.format: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer (JSON); CSV, GeoJSON, KML and shapefile downloads via Oregon GeoHub
sources.summary: Oregon's water-rights points of diversion, split into 39 queryable layers by source type and use, with priority date, use, rate in cfs, optional acre-feet and a link to each WRIS record.
sources.coverage_note: Oregon only. 200,693 point-of-diversion rows across 39 layers; current individually held rights only, with no status field.
caveats: Excludes irrigation-district rights, applications, transfers and leases.
Acre-feet is sparsely filled; no status field.

problems: The documented compilation procedures PDF on arcgis.wrd.state.or.us timed out (30-40 s), so procedures were not read.
Total is the sum of count queries over the 39 POD layers; distinct rights were not computed.

example.example_result: HTTP 200 JSON: certificate 16266, surface water, irrigation, priority date 1882-07-15, rate 0.3 cfs, 4.5 acre-feet, with a wris_link to the WRIS record.

members_summary.scope_note: Universe: the 39 Points of Diversion layers of the Water_Rights_by_Type_and_Use_WGS84 FeatureServer (the 39 Places of Use layers were not queried). All 39 were counted; layers 76, 64 and 104 were inspected field by field.
members_summary.pattern: 3 source types (Surface, Groundwater, Storage) x 13 use groups

sources.name: OWRD Water Rights Information Query (WRIS)
sources.format: HTML record pages (search by file ID, location, name or stream)
sources.summary: OWRD's per-right web records show the status of each Oregon water right, its points of diversion, places of use with priority date, decree or certificate reference and scanned documents.
sources.coverage_note: Oregon only; record-by-record viewer with search by file ID, location, name or stream. No bulk export was found.

problems: Only one record page was opened (linked from a GIS feature); search forms were not submitted.
No bulk download of the full WRIS table was found.

example.example_result: Certificate 16266, Josephine County: Status Non-Cancelled; POD on a creek; irrigation place of use of 15.0 acres with priority date 7/15/1882; decree reference. (Contact block exists; not reproduced.)

if_unstructured.summary: Record-by-record web pages exist where bulk data is thin: Oregon WRIS pages show status and place-of-use details; California describes CalWATRS as the system where holders view their own records (access conditions not tested).

local_terms.meaning: Legal entitlement to divert or use water, created and recorded by each state.
Location where water is taken from a source.
California's approved annual amount of a right, in acre-feet.
Doctrine ranking rights by priority date: first in time, first in right.
California right tied to land bordering a watercourse; often has no face value.
Colorado court-decreed use code and summed decreed amount, absolute or conditional.

provenance.note: Minutes are researcher estimates. Counts describe documented passes, not publication approval. Missing history or effort is not reconstructed.
